statusMeanings.accepted: Accepted as worth considering or to work on.

items.title: Gritty, grim realism
items.detail: Aim for a grim, gritty tone in the line of Another World, Abe's Oddysee and Splatterhouse, not a wacky, high-octane retro party game.

sources.quote: Take the game in the direction of like gritty realism
I wouldn't go making it all retro um high octane uh wild party game

items.title: Constant power-up spam for a high-octane feel
items.detail: Rejected: filling the game with frequent power-ups (as in Glyphblade) would make it wacky and high-octane; Andy says not to take the game in that direction.

sources.quote: power-ups like I put in um glyph blade like power up power
don't take the game in that direction
I think that would be kind of cool, like if you, like, to not make it silly, like vampire

items.title: Plot: a parasitic organism is taking over the city
items.detail: An alien parasite that bonds with organic life and machinery is spreading under the city; its origin (bioweapon or invader) is a matter of conspiracy theory. Most people think it is a myth; the military and authorities cover up surface outbreaks and steal the biological material. Answers Deano's request to flesh out the story.

sources.quote: the city is being taken over by a parasitic alien organism that is able to assimilate and bond with organic life as well as machinery
military and some authorities seem to be aware of whats going on but keep it under wraps
some fleshing out of story/plot

items.title: The player is a Hunter, an extraterrestrial
items.detail: The players are alien Hunters whose home world was ravaged by the parasite. They crashed on Earth and were captured; humans think they are the invaders. Their crew is small and time is short; they must fight through the city and into the depths to destroy the parasite.

sources.quote: you, the player, are an extraterrestrial
you are a Hunter.
your ship had at least 20 crew initially, who knows how many remain now

items.title: Three factions: Hunters, humans and the parasite
items.detail: Humans are as hostile to the Hunters as the parasite is, giving three factions in the fight. Deano asked for more than two factions for creative dynamics.

sources.quote: more than two factions for creative dynamics, the player, the human enemies, and the alien enemies
three factions caught up in the chaos, only you really trying to stop it

items.title: Level progression tells a story
items.detail: The order of levels and encounters should build a story and change as players go deeper; MVP progression was awkward. Retro: plan what the player meets in the first 30 seconds, the first minute, the midpoint and before the boss.

sources.quote: level progression is awkward, it needs to tell a story
graduated level progression
what the player meets in the first 30 seconds, first minute, midpoint, before the boss.

items.title: Four playable Hunter designs
items.detail: The character study has four Hunter designs: hunter1 (masked, cable head tendrils, industrial combat armour, large rifle), hunter2 (lean, sinewy, elongated predatory armoured head, digitigrade legs), hunter3 (compact, stocky, bare alien face; tendrils added and face made less reptilian at the user's request) and hunter4 (low, forward-leaning, swept-back carapace and powered exosuit).

sources.quote: Keep the same powerful non-human anatomy, masked head, sweeping cable tendrils, practical industrial combat armour, large rifle held in both hands
a lean, sinewy non-human alien hunter with an elongated predatory armoured head
Make its face less dinosaur/reptile-like, more distinctly alien and predatory
The character wears heavy armor and a powered exosuit

sources.shows: hunter1: masked alien hunter with cable head tendrils, heavy armour and a large rifle, right-facing
hunter4: low, forward-leaning hunter with a long snout and swept-back shell, in a rainy street

items.title: Hunter visual rules
items.detail: All Hunters share cable-like head tendrils, non-human predatory anatomy, practical industrial armour and a large two-handed gun, shown in a clear right-facing side-view silhouette. Variants change equipment and finish, not species.

sources.quote: Image 2 is a reference ONLY for the alien hunters' signature cable-like head tendrils.
This is a distinct design variation of the same hunter, not a new species.

items.title: Hunter equipment
items.detail: Each Hunter has armour with optic camo, a shoulder mount for a personal defensive weapon, strong arms for big guns, combat boots, a helmet with advanced targeting and a utility pack for passive enhancements.

a shoulder mount that can fit a personal defensive weapons

sources.quote: Lobby flow (host Start, guest Ready, invite link, drop-in)

items.title: Input as named actions; one input frame per player per tick
items.detail: Bind keys to named actions read as held, pressed or released. Build one input frame per player per simulation tick (actions plus aim angle); that frame goes over the network and into replays. Compute pressed edges per tick, not per render frame.

sources.quote: Build one input frame per player per simulation tick (actions plus an aim angle).

items.title: Asset spec and gap list before building
items.detail: Before building, list every asset and its source, and write the asset spec: sizes, grid, autotile cases, frame counts, fps, anchor and event points, emissive layer, naming, JSON metadata. Label code-drawn placeholders. The MVP art handover documents are a starting point.

sources.quote: Before building, list every asset the game needs and its source (supplied, to commission, code-drawn placeholder).
Write the asset spec first: sizes, 32 px grid (or whatever is chosen), autotile neighbour cases, frame counts, fps, anchor and event points, emissive layer, naming, JSON metadata.

items.title: Don't treat generated images as runtime assets
items.detail: Image generation produces illustrations, not registered sprite sheets; the character studies are large single illustrations. Treat them as concept art and produce runtime art with a pixel-art step or an artist, at least for tiles and animation.

sources.quote: Generated images are concept art. Runtime art needs an exact spec and an acceptance check.
Treat image generation as concept art; produce runtime art with a pixel-art step (e.g. Aseprite) or a human artist, at least for tiles and animation.

items.title: Art validator and animation preview
items.detail: Check each art delivery automatically (dimensions, grid alignment, transparent edges, frame count, anchors, metadata) and preview sprite sheets at game scale over the zone background.

sources.quote: Checks each delivered image against the spec: dimensions, grid alignment, transparent edges and halos, frame count, anchors, metadata present.
Plays a sprite sheet at game scale over the zone background with its anchor and ground line shown.

items.title: Depth, normal, mask and pose maps for sprites
items.detail: The character study keeps depth, normal, mask, pose and 3D-geometry estimates beside sprites (done for hunter1; hunter2 has a 3D estimate) and lists the tools that make them. How the game uses these maps is not stated.

sources.quote: dntrs-isde - generate depth map
dntrs-isne - generate normal map
generate moge 3d geometry estimation (produces a glb, a mask, a depth, and normals)

items.title: Character file naming: index-slug-type
items.detail: Name character files [index]-[slug]-[type].ext, with dashes between fields and underscores within a field; each entity has a unique index shared by its images and variants.

sources.quote: `[index]-[slug]-[type].ext`
Each entity has a unique index, shared by its images and variants.

items.title: Character source art: one right-facing figure on a transparent background
items.detail: Each study is one complete right-facing side-view figure with its weapon, on a transparent background, with no scenery, text or muzzle flash, and arms visibly connected to hands.

sources.quote: Show one right-facing full figure in a readable side-view, with the complete figure and weapon in frame. Transparent background, no scene, text, borders, other figures or muzzle flash.

items.title: A generation record beside every generated image
items.detail: Each generated study has a .generated.json record: prompt, references and their roles, generator, settings, and a separate post-generation visual analysis with defects.

sources.quote: "provenance": "Post-generation subagent visual analysis; not part of the original generation prompt."

items.title: Avoid losing which prompt made which image
items.detail: Some hunter variants were generated concurrently and the output was truncated, so their records list candidate prompts instead of the exact one. Record each prompt with its image.

sources.quote: The concurrent tool output was truncated, so the mapping between individual outputs and prompts could not be recovered.

items.title: Asset manifest, loader with progress, loud failure
items.detail: A manifest each module adds to, preloaded per zone, with a progress display and a clear error on a missing file.

sources.quote: A manifest that each module adds to, preloaded per zone, with a clear error on a missing file.

items.title: Hot reload of textures
items.detail: A dev key or Vite file watching reloads three.js textures in place, so art can be checked in the running game without a restart.

sources.quote: so art can be checked in the game without a restart

items.title: Bitmap HUD font with widths stored in the image
items.detail: A pixel font drawn in one PNG with character widths marked in its bottom row, so no separate metrics file is needed. Limited to ASCII from code 32.

sources.quote: A pixel HUD font that artists can draw in one PNG with no separate metrics file.

items.title: Don't reuse Biolab code or assets, or unlicensed Impact images
items.detail: Biolab Disaster has no licence: ideas only. Impact's font and collision-tile images have no stated licence. Impact and high_impact code is MIT: reuse only with the notice kept.

sources.quote: Treat as all rights reserved: ideas only.
Do not reuse without checking.
Code may be reused if the licence notice is kept.

items.title: Sound effects as data in one audio file
items.detail: Load one audio file of sound effects once and play sections of it; each sound is a data entry (start, end, one-shot or loop). Music is a separate item, T-091.

sources.quote: sound can be a single audio file loaded one time and we just granularly play and pick what we want. sounds then become pure data expressions (start, end, one-shoot or loop, etc)

items.notes: 2026-11-17, project owner: split this item in two; this one covers general audio (sound effects) and T-091 covers music.

items.title: Web Audio for effects, streamed music, unlock on first input
items.detail: Decode each effect once and play many times with Web Audio; stream music; unlock audio on the first input. Check current Safari codec support before choosing formats.

sources.quote: Web Audio for all effects (decode once, many plays), streamed music, a first-input unlock.

items.title: Don't add HTML5 Audio channel pools
items.detail: Impact's HTML5 Audio pools are a fallback for browsers without Web Audio; not needed now.

sources.quote: A fallback for browsers without Web Audio. Not needed now (judgement).

items.title: Regression tests that fail by default
items.detail: Strong regression tests; none is written without confirming it tests what it claims, and each fails by default.

sources.quote: strong regression tests, no tests get written without confirming they test what we want. fail by default

items.title: Don't let a test switch off what it tests
items.detail: MVP co-op tests made players invulnerable and the bot teleported past obstacles, so real bugs got through. Every hazard needs an "enter and leave" test.

sources.quote: Tests must not switch off the thing being tested.
A bot that cheats proves nothing about the level.
Every hazard needs an "enter and leave" test.

items.title: Debug overlay and frame-time graph
items.detail: Show hitboxes, the collision grid, entity IDs, network round trip, snapshot size and frame time, plus a rolling frame-time graph with network event marks (snapshot received, correction applied).

sources.quote: Hitboxes, entity IDs, network round trip, snapshot size, frame time.
Add net marks ("snapshot received", "correction applied") to the graph

items.title: Input recording and replay
items.detail: Record both players' inputs with the seed and replay the session exactly, for bugs one player saw once.

sources.quote: Records both players' inputs with the seed; replays the session exactly.

items.title: Two-client network test with injected lag
items.detail: Two tabs on one machine hide latency bugs. Run two headless clients with injected lag, loss and reordering in CI and check positions and events match.

sources.quote: Two tabs on one machine hide every latency bug. Inject lag and packet reordering in tests.
Two headless browsers with injected lag, loss and reordering; checks positions and events match.

items.title: Local-transport and lag test options
items.detail: Carry over ?net=local (two tabs without PeerJS) and ?lag=ms, which reproduced the stale-packet bug.

sources.quote: Co-op in two tabs without PeerJS or the internet.
Reproduced the stale-packet arena bug.

items.title: Reachability and placement checks for every level
items.detail: Keep the real-physics reachability check. Add a placement checker: lamps attached to a wall or ceiling, ladders join two floors, hazards have a source, enemies have enough floor, nothing spawns inside geometry.

sources.quote: Runs over every level: lamps attached to a wall or ceiling, ladders join two floors, hazards have a source, enemies have enough floor, nothing spawns inside geometry.
Real-physics reachability check (idea and approach)

items.title: Hazard run-through bot
items.detail: A bot that holds right and jumps, ignoring hazards, and reports hazard damage per section.

sources.quote: A bot that holds right and jumps, ignoring hazards; reports how much hazard damage it took per section.

items.title: Playtest telemetry
items.detail: Record deaths, time per section and damage per zone, plotted on the level, so difficulty is not tuned by feel or by bot.

sources.quote: Deaths, time per section and damage taken per zone, plotted on the level.

items.title: In-game feedback key and changelog
items.detail: One key saves a screenshot, zone, seed, position, version and a typed note; a changelog next to the version label tells testers what to look at.

sources.quote: One key saves a screenshot, zone, seed, position, version and a typed note to a file or clipboard.
next to the version label, so testers know what to look at.

items.title: Shared library of reusable code
items.detail: Keep code DRY (don't repeat yourself) and maintain a shared library of reusable code.

sources.quote: keep code DRY, maintain a shared library of reusable code

items.title: Pure functions, functional and modular build
items.detail: Keep functions pure and the build as functional as possible while modular.

sources.quote: try to keep functions pure, try to keep the general build as functional as possible while being modular

items.title: Don't build a custom module loader or class system
items.detail: Use native ES modules and classes; Impact's system deep-copies every property on construction and hides allocation costs.

sources.quote: Native ES modules and classes do this with tooling support. The deep copy hides allocation costs.

items.title: Don't extend built-in prototypes
items.detail: Global side effects can conflict with libraries such as three.js and PeerJS. Use plain helper functions.

sources.quote: Global side effects that can conflict with libraries (three.js, PeerJS). Use plain helper functions.

items.title: Don't look up entity classes by global name
items.detail: Fragile and pollutes the global scope. Use an explicit registry from type id to definition, which also lists entities for the editor and for checking level files.

sources.quote: Use an explicit registry from type id to definition

items.title: Bundle with Vite or esbuild
items.detail: Use Vite or esbuild for dependency-ordered bundling and minification.

sources.quote: Use Vite or esbuild, which do this.

items.title: Deploy workflow with a visible version stamp
items.detail: Carry over the Pages workflow that writes a version stamp, and show the version label so every player's build is known.

sources.quote: Pages workflow with version stamp
and the protocol check made it obvious which build each player had.

items.title: One-purpose changes with checks before each playtest
items.detail: For each change: update the spec, build it in a one-purpose commit, run the bot, reachability, placement and lag tests, deploy, check the version label, playtest with the checklist, triage feedback.

sources.quote: Build the change in a small commit with one purpose.

items.title: One owner per folder
items.detail: Each session (code, art, sound, docs) owns its own folder; handovers have acceptance criteria.

sources.quote: Handovers are contracts with acceptance criteria.

items.title: Record asset licences in the repository
items.detail: Record the licence of every third-party or self-made asset pack in the repository.

sources.quote: for every third-party or self-made asset pack.

items.title: Restore the MVP's original low-health heartbeat
items.detail: Use the old heartbeat sound, which Deano found acceptable, instead of the rejected bfxr replacement.

sources.quote: the old one was ok
Restore the old heartbeat; audition step.

items.title: Interpolate between simulation states when drawing
items.detail: Draw a blend of the previous and current simulation state using alpha = accumulator / dt, so motion does not stutter when the display rate and the step rate differ. It must work with pixel-stable rendering (T-005): interpolate first, then snap what is drawn to the pixel grid. That combination is not yet tested.

sources.quote: causing a subtle but visually unpleasant stuttering
alpha = accumulator / dt

items.title: Cap frame time or steps per frame
items.detail: Clamp each frame's elapsed time (the article uses 0.25 s) or cap the number of simulation steps per frame, so one slow frame cannot make the loop fall further behind every frame (the "spiral of death"). Under heavy load the game slows down instead.

sources.quote: It's called the spiral of death because being behind causes your update to simulate more steps to catch up
clamp at a maximum # of steps per-frame and the simulation will appear to slow down under heavy load
if ( frameTime > 0.25 ) frameTime = 0.25;

items.title: Music in the best supported format, with song sections
items.detail: Play music in the most efficient format the browser supports: Ogg preferred, MP3 as the fallback, chosen by a support check at run time. A song can define named sections (for example intro, loop, transition) so sections can loop and the music can change dynamically. Specifics to be decided.
items.notes: 2026-11-17, project owner: split from T-066 (general audio). Music should be in the most efficient supported format (Ogg preferred, with MP3 and Ogg support checks), and songs need a way to define sections for looping sections, dynamic music and transitions; specifics to be decided.
